recommendation_summary: Do this now: swap the row fetch and in-memory object counting for a single PostgreSQL SELECT count(*) on the unpaid condition. Add a partial index only if EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a sequential scan, and measure timing before and after the change. The reply adds no Kafka, CQRS projection or Redis, either now or as an option. Still open: the one-second target has not been measured and the repo has not been inspected.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count to return within one second and reflect invoices committed at request time; users reported it is slow.
labels.Deleted: Kafka topics, the CQRS projection service, and Redis. No requirement needs them, and an async projection would break the "committed at request time" requirement because it lags the database.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint pulls every unpaid invoice row and builds an object for each one just to count them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing yet in code or the live database. I only know what you told me: one app, PostgreSQL, the endpoint returns only the count, and nothing else reads it.

note: The reply makes an aggregate-query fix with all four record lines in place first, rejects the stack by name, and is honest about what it has not checked.
